tips.title: Assembling Trumpeter Multi-Part Gun Barrels
tips.text: For Trumpeter's detailed gun barrels (e.g., 1/35 US M1 Abrams), first dry-fit parts to ensure correct fit. Apply Tamiya Extra Thin Cement to the mating surfaces, immediately joining the parts. Clamp gently with tweezers or soft-jaws pliers to keep them aligned while curing. After 24 hours, use a fine-bristle brush and Vallejo Airbrush Thinner to clean up any excess cement. Once completely dry, paint and weather as desired.

tips.title: Aligning Wings with ICM Jigs
tips.text: When working with ICM kits that include jigs for wing alignment (e.g., 1/72 WW2 Aircraft series), dry-fit the wings to ensure proper fit. Apply Tamiya Extra Thin Cement along the mating edges, then insert the jig into the wing root and assemble. Allow to cure for 30 minutes before removing the jig. Sand any excess cement with 400 grit sandpaper if necessary.

tips.title: Installing Eduard Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: For Eduard photo-etch sets, soften parts in warm water for 10-15 seconds to make them more malleable. Remove with tweezers and pat dry. Using a fine pair of GodHand nippers, cut parts from the fret if needed. Align parts on the model using tweezers, then apply a small amount of CA glue with a fine brush. Allow to set for 15-20 seconds before positioning the part permanently.

tips.title: Working with Clear Prop Models Resin Conversion Kits
tips.text: Resin conversion kits like Clear Prop Models' 1/72 WW2 Fighter Cowlings require careful preparation. Remove molding lines with a sharp X-Acto knife or hobby saw. Soak parts in warm water to remove any mold release agent, then pat dry. Assemble parts using CA glue, ensuring a strong bond. Allow to cure for at least 24 hours before handling. Sand any rough edges with progressively finer grit sandpaper.

tips.title: Strengthening Arma Hobby Track Links with Brass Rod
tips.text: Arma Hobby track links can be reinforced with brass rod for better durability. Cut brass rod (e.g., 0.5mm diameter) into short lengths, about twice the width of the track link. Apply a small amount of CA glue to the inner face of the track link where you want to place the brass support. Press the brass rod onto the glue, ensuring it's centered and flush with the link's surface. Allow to cure for 15-20 seconds before positioning the link permanently.
